_comment: Deployed API mode — server reads private repos via GITHUB_TOKEN (env var, never in the browser). Pair with GitHub Pages frontend using VITE_API_URL.

github._backlogsComment: Vault-native: each entry names a space and the server reads <space>/{raw,wiki,output}/*.md plus <space>/sprints/*.md from the `vault` repo above (ADR-MOS-01/04/06). Omit owner/repo/path to default to that repo and the space's own directory; set them to read a space from a different repo. An entry whose `path` ends in .json instead reads a pre-built backlog document, for a deployment still on a mirror.

memory._comment: Optional. Same topology contract as instance.config.json's 'memory' block, read over the GitHub content API instead of the local FS. Omit this whole block and memory falls back to the default: the instance repo's own memory/{raw,wiki,output} as the sole canon root plus the vault repo's top-level dirs as federated mounts — byte-for-byte the prior behaviour. Each root/federated entry takes an optional 'repo' (instance | vault | framework, default instance) naming which repo above it lives in, since a deployed server can only reach repos it has owner/repo/ref for; 'path' is relative to that repo's root. 'roots' are canon (counted as the raw→wiki→output pipeline); each has a 'layout' of flat | tier/project | project/tier. 'federated' mounts are navigation context, never counted as canon. ${var} expands here exactly as in backlogs. Broken/missing roots or mounts, or an unknown 'repo' label, are skipped and reported (topology.skipped), never fatal.
